entries.text: ElectriCraft carries shaft power as electricity over wires. A generator turns shaft power into voltage and current, wires carry it, and a motor at the other end turns it back into shaft power. Voltage follows the generator's speed, current its torque. Use this book while looking at an ElectriCraft block to open its page.

Wires join into a network. Each metal has its own current limit and resistance: steel and tin carry little, copper, silver and gold much more, and superconductors carry anything with no loss. Too much current melts a wire into lava. Insulated and bare wires of a metal carry the same.
entries.title: Wires

entries.text: Takes shaft power on its front and feeds the wire network at its back: the voltage is eight times the speed, the current an eighth of the torque. It explodes far above 400 MW. The screwdriver turns it.

Takes current from the network and drives the machine at its back: the torque is eight times the current, the speed an eighth of the voltage. With several motors on one network, each only takes its share; an amplifier (red gold, tungsten or bedrock ingots) lets one draw more. Wool next to it makes it quieter.

Steps voltage up or down with the turns ratio set in its GUI, trading voltage for current. It loses a little, warms up with the power it carries, and explodes when it carries too much current or gets too hot.

Batteries charge from the network on every side but the top and, with a redstone signal, give out a fixed voltage and current from the top. Six tiers, from redstone to nether star; the charge stays on the item when broken.
entries.title: Batteries

entries.text: Limits the current that passes through it to the value of its coloured bands (two digits and a multiplier). Right-click a band with a dye to change it.
A resistor with three digits for finer values.
Conducts only while it has a redstone signal.
Burns out for good when the current goes over its rating; replace it afterwards.
Shows the voltage and current flowing through it and gives a comparator signal for the power.
A cable for Forge Energy (FE) that links energy blocks of any mod; right-click it to set the network's limit.
A huge FE store: it takes energy on every side but the top and gives it out of the top, pushing it upwards with a redstone signal.
The energy crystal used to build the FE battery.
Wireless chargers pass FE from their sides to the energy block two blocks in front of them. Higher tiers move more and lose less.
entries.title: Wireless Chargers

entries.text: ElectriCraft adds ores for tin, silver, nickel, aluminum and platinum; their ingots make the wires.
entries.title: Ores

entries.text: Dusts and crystals for batteries and parts: blue, diamond, quartz and crystal dust.
entries.title: Dusts

entries.text: Battery crystals hold the charge of a battery tier and are crafted into it.
